title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 20 | Week 11 vs. Kansas City Chiefs
headline: Carson Beck (back spasms) did not practice and is trending toward missing Sunday vs. KC. ARI is planning for Josh Johnson to start.
summary: Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck's back spasms flared up again and he did not practice Friday. LaFleur won't rule him out, but the team is preparing as if Josh Johnson starts Sunday against Kansas City. He is taking Beck's status "one minute at a time" and said it depends on how he responds to treatment and how he feels tomorrow. LaFleur doesn't think it will be a multi-week issue, but he wouldn't commit to that. He said he would be disappointed not to see Beck make a second start. He has called plays for Johnson before, had a great experience, and spoke warmly of Johnson as a veteran QB-room presence who can still throw. The offense is effectively back to the start of the playbook, with no "next step" in the install, and LaFleur says he is focused on getting the ball moving and on the defense and special teams. The rookie QB Joey (likely from Jacksonville's roster) is also in the mix and "will be ready," and a separate QB is being readied as the emergency third. LaFleur also called the remaining seven weeks an evaluation period for players and coaches.

He was asked about the five-game losing streak and said he won't give specifics, only that the staff is always looking for better ways to operate. He described the week as a test of his first year as head coach, with every decision based on what is best for the team. He praised defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver as a great coach who runs the meetings and builds confidence while holding players accountable. On the short week, he said practices were less physical but he liked the team's mental response and preparation. He said Carolina's defense under Todd Wash has simplified, playing fewer personnel groupings and fronts, living in nickel, and playing faster and more aggressively. Asked about Marlon Humphrey, he said he expects him to be there Monday, though the question's wording leaves his availability vague. He closed by stressing technique and mental intensity in walk-throughs to produce physical play on Sundays.

title: HC Sean Payton ahead of Week 11: ‘To get where we want to go, there has to be improvement’
headline: Sean Payton gave no injury or role updates for Week 11 at Las Vegas, but Riley Moss's extension is done and Denver wants better run-game efficiency and fewer explosive plays allowed.
summary: Payton opened by saying Friday's practice moved indoors because of forecast high winds, and he already knew what he wanted to teach that day. Most of the session was about Riley Moss's new contract. Payton praised his transition skills, instincts, length and compete level, and said he and George Paton felt they saw a corner when they drafted him. He said Moss's role is year to year, and that Ja'Quan McMillian-type flexibility doesn't apply here. He did say the Broncos have not discussed moving Patrick Surtain II to safety, and that Surtain can play outside or in dime. On Las Vegas, he praised Brock Bowers as a savvy tight end with transition skills, said Maxx Crosby's disruption makes the Tuesday and Wednesday meetings longer, and noted Crosby is off the field only 6% of the time this year. He credited the home crowd with causing in-huddle stress, citing the Kansas City false start as the difference in that game. He stressed ball security (the team has among the fewest giveaways) and said the team is looking at more reps to fix an inefficient run game. He also said the team must keep improving in every phase despite the strong record, and that there is still "meat on the bone." He gave no injury news on any Denver players.

title: Campbell on Clark being named captain
headline: Kerby Joseph returns Sunday vs. TB after 13 months out, but Campbell is tempering expectations. Expect rust and a workload he will assess after the game; Chuck Clark was named captain and is a key piece of the safety group.
summary: Campbell opened by saying Chuck Clark was named a captain two days ago. He praised Clark's leadership, communication and rising production, and called him a 'bellcow' for the defense. On Kerby Joseph's return, Campbell said there will be rust, because it is his first game in about 13 months, and he does not want anyone expecting a spectacular performance. He wants Joseph to play within the system and not try to do too much. How Joseph feels after roughly 45-55 reps will determine what comes next. Asked about the deep safety group, Campbell said the team has many packages and a role for every safety, and he did not say it is moving to a nickel-heavy base. He praised Tay Martin as a special teams staple who is also growing as a receiver. He said Tyleik Williams is playing nose as well as anyone in the league, citing his athleticism, smarts and pass-rush ability. He said linebackers have been given a lot, that it has slowed things at times, and that the team wants to spread the load across more defenders. He described the stretch of games (Germany, a short week, then Thanksgiving) as a mental-focus period, with walkthrough-heavy practices to keep players fresh before ramping up again after Thanksgiving.

title: Liam Coen on Readiness for Giants, Bates and Davis to Make Debuts | Press Conference
headline: Trevor Lawrence is playing with strong rhythm and accuracy, and Jonah Monheim starts on the road at the Giants with new defensive additions debuting.
summary: Coen called it a good, physical week of practice before Sunday's game at the Giants. He expects the two new defensive additions, whom the captions render as 'Jordan' and 'Jesse', to play, though how much depends on how the game flows. He said the safety seems dialed in on back-end communication. Most of the press conference was praise for Trevor Lawrence, who is processing quickly, playing the game slow, and placing the ball well. Coen pointed to the Josh Cameron touchdown as an example of clicking through progressions, and said the offense wants all eligibles to be threats on every play. title: Sean McVay discusses injury updates, evolving the Rams' offense, preparing for Week 12 & more

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: November 20, 2026
headline: Joe Milton III is now Philadelphia's starting QB, and the struggling offense is being streamlined after the bye. Expect simpler communication and a base-plan reset, not a full overhaul.
summary: Sirianni said the offense keeps a base plan built in OTAs and training camp, then adapts it to what the players do well. He admitted the offense hasn't played or coached well enough and used the bye week to dig deeper into why things were or weren't working, which let the staff streamline further. On the new quarterback, he stressed that reps matter, including calling the play in the huddle and getting everyone lined up, and that Joe Milton III is getting those in practice, walkthroughs and post-practice developmental periods. He also noted the communication between Milton and Sean (apparently the QB coach) counts as extra practice. On the defensive tackle room, he declined to concede a drop-off after the Jordan Davis move the reporter referenced, saying he has a lot of faith in the depth and development there. He called the week business as usual, said Thursday's practice had good intensity, effort and fundamentals, and said the team is in a good spot on the same page. Questions about Zach Ertz's franchise records and the pre-draft evaluation of a rookie (the name was garbled in the captions) got generic answers with nothing actionable. No injury updates or specific role changes for skill players were given.

Asked about getting Calvin Ridley more involved, he spoke only about Ridley's attitude and leadership with the young players and gave no usage plan. He praised Jacob Martin's career-best sack season, his selflessness and his veteran leadership. The rest of the session was mostly about Solomon Thomas' character and the mental challenges young players face in the NFL.
